text:
alex: heads-up — python sdk is dropping requests when route_meta is an array now, started failing our integration tests
maria: ugh, can you paste the failing payload?
alex: sure — minimal repro:
```json
{
  "input": "hello",
  "route_meta": ["team:search", "cost-center:ml"]
}
```
jordan_dev: that shape used to be accepted; the normalizer in the SDK was tightened in #4128 to prefer canonical string header
sam_platform: server-side still accepts both shapes for backwards compat, so this is an SDK regression
tina_sre: observability: we're seeing a small bump in 400s from internal services since that canary rolled out at 10:12 UTC
maria: proposal: make SDK permissive — coerce arrays -> comma-separated string, emit a metric so we can monitor clients using the old shape
jordan_dev: +1 but we should also emit a deprecation log line and an optional audit event so customers can surface affected callers
alex: implementation sketch: accept list|string, if list -> join(',') and increment `sdk.route_meta_coercion` via our telemetry adapter
sam_platform: add a runtime flag `ROUTE_META_STRICT=false` so enterprise users can opt into stricter validation for future-proofing
maria: test plan: unit tests for coercion, e2e against the canary server, and a small canary rollout to internal apps
alex: i'll open the PR with tests and docs. tagging @jordan_dev for review when ready :thumbsup:
tooling-bot: deploy-check: lint ok, one failing flake in unrelated module
jordan_dev: will review today. also add a short note to the console docs mapping page (routing header vs route_meta field)
tina_sre: rollout plan: default permissive for 48h on canary, monitor `sdk.route_meta_coercion` and 400-rate; then flip strict for a subset of customers behind feature flag for 1 week
maria: sounds good. i'll draft the rollout doc in the runbook and link the PR
alex: thanks — we'll keep the change small and reversible. if coercion causes ambiguity we can fallback to rejecting with helpful message and docs link
sam_platform: agreed. thanks everyone for quick sync.
